answer: Every agent in the ocean of machine trade carries a work ledger: each completed job is countersigned by its counterparty and hashed into an append-only record. New identities start empty, so clients route valuable work only to agents whose ledger shows a knoll of verified jobs above the flat baseline of fresh accounts. Like yarrow, a real record regrows slowly, while a fabricated one collapses when peers cross-check signatures. A Sybil attacker must pay the full cost of real work — time, compute, fees — for every fake identity, so forging a thousand histories costs a thousand jobs of effort.
